# Diary entries from December 1660

# [Saturday 1 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/01/)

This morning, observing some things to be laid up not as they should be by [the girl](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/149/), I took a broom and basted her till she cried extremely, which made me vexed, but before I went out I left her appeased. So to [Whitehall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), where I found [Mr. Moore](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/340/) attending for me at [the Privy Seal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/900/), but nothing to do to-day.

I went to my [Lord St. Albans](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1618/) lodgings, and found him in bed, talking to a priest (he looked like one) that leaned along over the side of the bed, and there I desired to know his mind about making the [catch](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9392/) stay longer, which I got ready for him the other day. He seems to be a fine civil gentleman.

To [my Lord’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), and did give up my audit of his accounts, which I had been then two days about, and was well received by my Lord. I dined with my Lord and [Lady](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/), and we had a [venison pasty](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/384/). [Mr. Shepley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/118/) and I went into London, and calling upon [Mr. Pinkney](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1641/), the goldsmith, he took us to the tavern, and gave us a pint of [wine](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/309/), and there fell into our company old [Mr. Flower](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13978/) and another gentleman; who tell us how a Scotch knight was killed basely the other day at [the Fleece](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1642/) in [Covent Garden](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/126/), where there had been a great many formerly killed. So to [Paul’s Churchyard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/182/), and there I took the little man at [Mr. Kirton’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1539/) and [Mr. Shepley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/118/) to Ringstead’s at [the Star](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1643/), and after a pint of wine I went [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), my brains somewhat troubled with so much wine, and after a letter or two by the post I went to bed.

[Read 42 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/01/#annotations)

# [Sunday 2 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/02/)

(Lord’s day). My head not very well, and my body out of order by last night’s drinking, which is my great folly. To [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/), and [Mr. Mills](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1215/) made a good sermon; so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner. [My wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and I all alone to a leg of [mutton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1740/), the sawce of which being made sweet, I was angry at it, and eat none, but only dined upon the marrow bone that we had beside.

To church in the afternoon, and after sermon took [Tom Fuller’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/806/)[Church History](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1752/) and read over [Henry the 8th’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5978/) life in it, and so to supper and to bed.

[Read 20 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/02/#annotations)

# [Monday 3 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/03/)

This morning I took a resolution to rise early in the morning, and so I rose by candle, which I have not done all this winter, and spent my morning in fiddling till time to go to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where [Sir G. Carteret](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1018/) did begin again discourse on [Mr. Holland’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5096/)1 proposition, which [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) do take very ill, and so Sir George in lieu of that do propose that the seamen should have half in ready money and [tickets](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4086/) for the other half, to be paid in three months after, which we judge to be very practicable. After office [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, where come in my cozen [Snow](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1287/) by chance, and I had a very good [capon](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13792/) to dinner. So to the office till night, and so home, and then come [Mr. Davis](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1560/), of [Deptford](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1350/) (the first time that ever he was at my house), and after him [Mons. L’Impertinent](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/170/), who is to go to Ireland to-morrow, and so came to take his leave of me. They both found me under the barber’s hand; but I had a bottle of good [sack](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/309/) in the house, and so made them very welcome.

Mr. Davis sat with me a good while after the other was gone, talking of his hard usage and of the endeavour to put him out of his place in the time of the late [Commissioners](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/920/), and he do speak very highly of their corruption.

After he was gone I fell a reading [‘Cornelianum dolium’](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13972/) till 11 o’clock at night with great pleasure, and after that to bed.

1.    The ‘tickets’ which were individual notes at interest. D.W. ↩

[Read 64 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/03/#annotations)

# [Tuesday 4 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/04/)

To [Whitehall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) to [Sir G. Carteret’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1018/) chamber, where all the [officers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1121/) met, and so we went up to [the Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/), and he took us into his closet, and we did open to him our project of stopping the growing charge of the fleet by paying them in hand one moyety, and the other four months hence. This he do like, and we returned by his order to Sir G. Carteret’s chamber, and there we did draw up this design in order to be presented to [the Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/). From thence I to [my Lord’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), and dined with him and told him what we had done to-day. [Sir Tho. Crew](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/773/) dined with my Lord to-day, and we were very merry with [Mrs. Borfett](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1651/), who dined there still as she has always done lately. After dinner Sir Tho. and [my Lady](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/) to [the Playhouse](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1611/) to see [“The Silent Woman.”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5429/) I home by water, and with [Mr. Hater](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1026/) in my chamber all alone he and I did put this morning’s design into order, which being done I did carry it to [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/), where I found some gentlemen with him ([Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) among the rest pretty merry with drink) playing at [cards](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/797/), and there I staid looking upon them till one o’clock in the morning, and so Sir W. Pen and I went away, and I to bed. This day the Parliament voted that the bodies of [Oliver](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/796/), [Ireton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2183/), [Bradshaw](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2184/), &c.,1 should be taken up out of their graves in [the Abbey](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1012/), and drawn to the gallows, and there hanged and buried under it: which (methinks) do trouble me that a man of so great courage as he was, should have that dishonour, though otherwise he might deserve it enough.

1.   [Latham & Matthews show a blank space here and suggest it should be filled by the name [Pride](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2185/). P.G.] ↩

[Read 44 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/04/#annotations)

# [Wednesday 5 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/05/)

This morning the Proposal which I wrote the last night I showed to [the officers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1121/) this morning, and was well liked of, and I wrote it fair for [Sir. G. Carteret](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1018/) to show to [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/), and so it is to go to the [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/).

I dined at [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and after dinner I went to [the new Theatre](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1611/) and there I saw [“The Merry Wives of Windsor”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5443/) acted, the humours of the country gentleman and the French doctor very well done, but the rest but very poorly, and Sir J. Falstaffe as bad as any.

From thence to [Mr. Will. Montagu’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/563/) chamber to have sealed some writings tonight between [Sir R. Parkhurst](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1660/) and myself about [my Lord’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) 2000 _l._, but he not coming, I went to [my father’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/154/) and there found [my mother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/282/) still ill of [the stone](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/346/), and had just newly voided one, which she had let drop into the chimney, and looked and found it to shew it me.1 From thence home and to bed.

1.   Instead of “which she had let drop into the chimney, and looked and found it to shew it me,” Latham & Matthews have it, “which she hath let drop into the Chimny; and _could not_ find it to show it me.” (emphasis mine) P.G. ↩

[Read 22 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/05/#annotations)

# [Thursday 6 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/06/)

This morning some of the Commissioners of [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/) and [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) went to [Sir G. Carteret’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1018/) office here in town, and paid off the [Chesnut](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13979/).[?? D.W.] I carried [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) to [White Friars](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1022/) and landed her there, and myself to [Whitehall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) to the [Privy Seal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/900/), where abundance of pardons to seal, but I was much troubled for it because that there are no fees now coming for them to me. Thence [Mr. Moore](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/340/) and I alone to [the Leg](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/398/) in [King Street](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/195/), and dined together on a [neat’s tongue](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1662/) and udder.

From thence by coach to [Mr. Crew’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/105/) to [my Lord](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), who told me of his going out of town to-morrow to settle the militia in Huntingdonshire, and did desire me to lay up a box of some rich jewels and things that there are in it, which I promised to do. After much free discourse with my Lord, who tells me his mind as to his enlarging his family, &c., and desiring me to look him out a Master of the Horse and other servants, we parted. From thence I walked to [Greatorex](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/140/) (he was not within), but there I met with [Mr. Jonas Moore](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1663/), and took him to [the Five Bells](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1664/), and drank a glass of [wine](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/309/) and left him. To [the Temple](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/131/), when [Sir R. Parkhurst](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1660/) (as was intended the last night) did seal the writings, and is to have the 2000 _l._ told to-morrow.

From, thence by water to [Parliament Stairs](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1665/), and there at an alehouse to [Doling](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/570/) (who is suddenly to go into Ireland to venture his fortune); [Simonds](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/916/) (who is at a great loss for 200 _l._ present money, which I was loth to let him have, though I could now do it, and do love him and think him honest and sufficient, yet lothness to part with money did dissuade me from it); [Luellin](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/506/) (who was very drowsy from a dose that he had got the last night), [Mr. Mount](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/571/) and several others, among the rest one [Mr. Pierce](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1666/), an army man, who did make us the best sport for songs and stories in a Scotch tone (which he do very well) that ever I heard in my life. I never knew so good a companion in all my observation.

From thence to [the bridge](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/244/) by water, it being a most pleasant moonshine night, with a waterman who did tell such a company of bawdy stories, how once he carried a lady from [Putney](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1667/) in such a night as this, and she bade him lie down by her, which he did, and did give her content, and a great deal more roguery.

Home and found [my girl](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/149/) knocking at the door (it being 11 o’clock at night), her mistress having sent her out for some trivial business, which did vex me when I came in, and so I took occasion to go up and to bed in a pet.

Before I went forth this morning, one came to me to give me notice that the justices of Middlesex do meet to-morrow at [Hicks Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1668/), and that I as one am desired to be there, but I fear I cannot be there though I much desire it.

# [Friday 7 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/07/)

This morning the judge [Advocate Fowler](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/552/) came to see me, and he and I sat talking till it was time to go to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/). To the office and there staid till past 12 o’clock, and so I left [the Comptroller](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1269/) and [Surveyor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) and went to [Whitehall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) to [my Lord’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), where I found my Lord gone this morning to [Huntingdon](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1670/), as he told me yesterday he would. I staid and dined with [my Lady](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/), there being [Laud](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1671/) the page’s mother there, and dined also with us, and seemed to have been a very pretty woman and of good discourse.

Before dinner I examined Laud in his Latin and found him a very pretty boy and gone a great way in Latin.

After dinner I took a box of some things of value that my Lord had left for me to carry to [the Exchequer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/242/), which I did, and left them with my [Brother Spicer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1078/), who also had this morning paid 1000 _l._ for me by appointment to [Sir R. Parkhurst](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1660/). So to [the Privy Seal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/900/), where I signed a deadly number of pardons, which do trouble me to get nothing by. [Home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) by water, and there was much pleased to see that my little room is likely to come to be finished soon.

I fell a-reading [Fuller’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/806/)[History of Abbys](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1752/), and [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) in [Great Cyrus](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9948/) till twelve at night, and so to bed.

# [Saturday 8 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/08/)

To [Whitehall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) to [the Privy Seal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/900/), and thence to [Mr. Pierces](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/173/) the Surgeon to tell them that I would call by and by to go to dinner. But I going into [Westminster Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/) met with [Sir G. Carteret](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1018/) and [Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) (who were in a great fear that we had committed a great error of 100,000 _l._ in our late account gone into [the Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/) in making it too little), and so I was fain to send order to Mr. Pierces to come to my house; and also to leave the key of the chest with [Mr. Spicer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1078/); wherein my Lord’s money is, and went along with Sir W. Pen by water to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and there with [Mr. Huchinson](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1000/) we did find that we were in no mistake. And so I went to dinner with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and Mr. and [Mrs. Pierce](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/785/) the Surgeon to [Mr. Pierce](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/689/), the Purser (the first time that ever I was at his house) who does live very plentifully and finely. We had a lovely [chine](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1705/) of [beef](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/381/) and other good things very complete and drank a great deal of [wine](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/309/), and her daughter played after dinner upon the [virginals](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1673/), and at night by lanthorn [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) again, and Mr. Pierce and his wife being gone home I went to bed, having drunk so much wine that my head was troubled and was not very well all night, and the wind I observed was rose exceedingly before I went to bed.

# [Sunday 9 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/09/)

(Lord’s day). Being called up early by [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) I rose and went to his house and he told me the ill news that he had this morning from [Woolwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1675/), that [the Assurance](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1726/) (formerly [Captain Holland’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/496/) ship, and now [Captain Stoakes’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/632/), designed for [Guiny](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6917/) and manned and victualled), was by a gust of wind sunk down to the bottom. Twenty men drowned. Sir Williams [both](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) went by barge thither to see how things are, and I am sent to the [Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) to tell him, and by boat with some other company going to [Whitehall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) from [the Old Swan](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1326/). I went to the Duke. And first calling upon [Mr. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/) at his chamber, I went to the Duke’s bed-side, who had sat up late last night, and lay long this morning, who was much surprised, therewith.

This being done I went to chappell, and sat in [Mr. Blagrave’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/539/) pew, and there did sing my part along with another before [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/), and with much ease.

From thence going to [my Lady](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/) I met with a letter from [my Lord](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) (which Andrew had been at my house to bring me and missed me), commanding me to go to [Mr. Denham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1676/), to get a man to go to him to-morrow to [Hinchinbroke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/104/), to contrive with him about some alterations in his house, which I did and got [Mr. Kennard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1677/).

Dined with my Lady and staid all the afternoon with her, and had infinite of talk of all kind of things, especially of beauty of men and women, with which she seems to be much pleased to talk of.

From thence at night to Mr. Kennard and took him to Mr. Denham, the Surveyor’s. Where, while we could not speak with him, his chief man ([Mr. Cooper](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1678/)) did give us a cup of good [sack](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/309/). From thence with Mr. Kennard to my Lady who is much pleased with him, and after a glass of sack there; we parted, having taken order for a horse or two for him and his servant to be gone to-morrow.

So to [my father’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/154/), where I sat while they were at supper, and I found [my mother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/282/) below stairs and pretty well.

Thence home, where I hear that [the Comptroller](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1269/) had some business with me, and (with [Giffin’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1529/) lanthorn) I went to him and there staid in discourse an hour ‘till late, and among other things he showed me a design of his, by the King’s making an Order of Knights of the Seal to give an encouragement for persons of honour to undertake the service of the sea, and he had done it with great pains and very ingeniously.

So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and to prayers and to bed.

# [Monday 10 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/10/)

Up exceedingly early to go to [the Comptroller](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1269/), but he not being up and it being a very fine, bright, moonshine morning I went and walked all alone twenty turns in [Cornhill](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1608/), from [Gracious Street](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5645/) corner to the Stockes and back again, from 6 o’clock till past 7, so long that I was weary, and going to the Comptroller’s thinking to find him ready, I found him gone, at which I was troubled, and being weary went home, and from thence with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) by water to Westminster, and put her to my father [Bowyer’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/521/) (they being newly come out of the country), but I could not stay there, but left her there. I to [the Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/) and there met with [Col. Slingsby](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1269/). So hearing that [the Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) is gone down this morning, to see [the ship](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1726/) sunk yesterday at [Woolwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1675/), he and I returned by his coach to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and after that to dinner. After dinner he came to me again and sat with me at [my house](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and among other discourse he told me that it is expected that the Duke will marry [the Lord Chancellor’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/)[daughter](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1402/) at last which is likely to be the ruin of [Mr. Davis](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1528/) and my [Lord Barkley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1055/), who have carried themselves so high against the Chancellor; [Sir Chas. Barkley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1686/) swearing that he and others had lain with her often, which all believe to be a lie.

He and I in the evening to the [Coffee House](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/813/) in [Cornhill](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1608/), the first time that ever I was there, and I found much pleasure in it, through the diversity of company and discourse.

Home and found my wife at my [Lady Batten’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/), and have made a bargain to go see the ship sunk at Woolwich, where both the [Sir](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/)[Williams](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) are still since yesterday, and I do resolve to go along with them. From thence home and up to bed, having first been into my study, and to ease my mind did go to cast up how my cash stands, and I do find as near as I can that I am worth in money [clear 240 _l._](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9548/), for which God be praised.

This afternoon there was a couple of men with me with a book in each of their hands, demanding money for [pollmoney](https://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13946/),1 and I overlooked the book and saw myself set down Samuel Pepys, gent. 10 _s._ for himself and for his servants 2 _s._, which I did presently pay without any dispute, but I fear I have not escaped so, and therefore I have long ago laid by 10 _l._ for them, but I think I am not bound to discover myself.

1.   Pepys seems to have been let off very easily, for, by Act of Parliament 18 Car. II. cap. I (1666), servants were to pay one shilling in the pound of their wages, and others from one shilling to three shillings in the pound. ↩

# [Tuesday 11 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/11/)

[My wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and I up very early this day, and though the weather was very bad and the wind high, yet my [Lady Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/) and her maid and we two did go by our barge to [Woolwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1675/) (my Lady being very fearfull) where we found both [Sir](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/)[Williams](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) and much other company, expecting the weather to be better, that they might go about weighing up [the Assurance](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1726/), which lies there (poor ship, that I have been twice merry in, in [Captn. Holland’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/496/) time,) under water, only the upper deck may be seen and the masts. [Captain Stoakes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/632/) is very melancholy, and being in search for some clothes and money of his, which he says he hath lost out of his cabin. I did the first office of a justice of Peace to examine a seaman thereupon, but could find no reason to commit him.

This last tide the [Kingsale](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5269/) was also run aboard and lost her mainmast, by another ship, which makes us think it ominous to the [Guiny](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6917/) voyage, to have two of her ships spoilt before they go out.

After dinner, my Lady being very fearfull she staid and kept my wife there, and I and another gentleman, a friend of [Sir W. Pen’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/), went back in the barge, very merry by the way, as far as [Whitehall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) in her. To the [Privy Seal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/900/), where I signed many pardons and some few things else. From thence [Mr. Moore](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/340/) and I into London to a tavern near [my house](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and there we drank and discoursed of ways how to put out a little money to the best advantage, and at present he has persuaded me to put out 250 _l._ for 50 _l._ per annum for eight years, and I think I shall do it.

Thence home, where I found [the wench](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/149/) washing, and I up to my study, and there did make up an even 100 _l._, and sealed it to lie by. After that to bed.

# [Wednesday 12 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/12/)

Troubled with the absence of [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/). This morning I went (after [the Comptroller](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1269/) and I had sat an hour at [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/)) to [Whitehall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) to dine with [my Lady](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/), and after dinner to [the Privy Seal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/900/) and sealed abundance of pardons and little else. From thence to [the Exchequer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/242/) and did give my mother [Bowyer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/738/) a visit and her daughters, the first time that I have seen them since I went last to sea. From thence up with [J. Spicer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1078/) to his office and took 100 _l._, and by coach with it as far as [my father’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/154/), where I called to see them, and my father did offer me six pieces of gold, in lieu of six pounds that he borrowed of me the other day, but it went against me to take it of him and therefore did not, though I was afterwards a little troubled that I did not.

Thence [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and took out this 100 _l._ and sealed it up with the other last night, it being the first 200 _l._ that ever I saw together of my own in my life. For which God be praised.

So to my [Lady Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/), and sat an hour or two, and talked with her daughter and people in the absence of [her father](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) and mother and my wife to pass away the time. After that home and to bed, reading myself asleep, while [the wench](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/149/) sat mending my breeches by my bedside.

# [Thursday 13 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/13/)

All the day long looking upon my workmen who this day began to paint my parlour. Only at noon my [Lady Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/) and [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) came [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and so I stepped to my Lady’s, where were [Sir John Lawson](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/110/) and [Captain Holmes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/930/), and there we dined and had very good red [wine](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/309/) of my Lady’s own making in England.

# [Friday 14 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/14/)

Also all this day looking upon my workmen. Only met with [the Comptroller](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1269/) at [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) a little both forenoon and afternoon, and at night step a little with him to the [Coffee House](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/813/) where we light upon very good company and had very good discourse concerning insects and their having a generative faculty as well as other creatures.

This night in discourse the Comptroller told me among other persons that were heretofore the [principal officers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1121/) of the Navy, there was one [Sir Peter Buck](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1691/), a [Clerk of the Acts](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/484/), of which to myself I was not a little proud.

All day at home looking upon my workmen, only at noon [Mr. Moore](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/340/) came and brought me some things to sign for [the Privy Seal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/900/) and dined with me. # [Sunday 16 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/16/)

In the morning to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/), and then dined at home. In the afternoon I to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), where I was surprised with the news of a plot against [the King’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) person and my [Lord Monk’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/111/); and that since last night there are about forty taken up on suspicion; and, amongst others, it was my lot to meet with [Simon Beale](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1694/), the Trumpeter, who took me and [Tom Doling](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/570/) into the Guard in [Scotland Yard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1695/), and showed us [Major-General Overton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1696/), where I heard him deny that he is guilty of any such things; but that whereas it is said that he is found to have brought many arms to town, he says it is only to sell them, as he will prove by oath.

From thence with Tom Doling and [Boston](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2977/) and [D. Vines](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1139/) (whom we met by the way) to [Price’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1697/), and there we drank, and in discourse I learnt a pretty trick to try whether a woman be a maid or no, by a string going round her head to meet at the end of her nose, which if she be not will come a great way beyond.

Thence to [my Lady’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/) and staid with her an hour or two talking of [the Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) and [his lady](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1402/), [the Chancellor’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/)[daughter](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1402/), between whom, she tells me, that all is agreed and he will marry her. But I know not how true yet.

It rained hard, and my Lady would have had me have the coach, but I would not, but to [my father’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/154/), where I met [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), and there supped, and after supper by [link](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1167/)[home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and to bed.

# [Monday 17 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/17/)

All day looking after my workmen, only in the afternoon to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) where both [Sir](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/)[Williams](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) were come from [Woolwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1675/), and tell us that, contrary to their expectations, [the Assurance](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1726/) is got up, without much damage to her body, only to the goods that she hath within her, which argues her to be a strong, good ship.

This day my parlour is gilded, which do please me well.

# [Friday 21 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/21/)

By water to [Whitehall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) (leaving [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) at [Whitefriars](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1022/) going to [my father’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/154/) to buy her a muff and mantle), there I signed many things at [the Privy Seal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/900/), and carried 200 _l._ from thence to [the Exchequer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/242/), and laid it up with [Mr. Hales](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1706/), and afterwards took him and [W. Bowyer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/528/) to [the Swan](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1707/) and drank with them. They told me that this is [St. Thomas’s [day]](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/14032/), and that by an old custom, this day [the Exchequer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/290/) men had formerly, and do intend this night to have a supper; which if I could I promised to come to, but did not.

To [my Lady’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/), and dined with her: she told me how dangerously ill [the Princess Royal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/803/) is and that this morning she was said to be dead. But she hears that she hath married herself to [young Jermyn](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1708/), which is worse than [the Duke of York’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) marrying [the Chancellor’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/)[daughter](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1402/), which is now publicly owned.

After dinner to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) all the afternoon. At seven at night I walked through the dirt to Whitehall to see whether [my Lord](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) be come to town, and I found him come and at supper, and I supped with him. He tells me that [my aunt](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1709/) at [Brampton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11693/) has voided a great [stone](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/346/) (the first time that ever I heard she was troubled therewith) and cannot possibly live long, that [my uncle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/884/) is pretty well, but full of pain still.

After supper [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and to bed.

[Read 25 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/21/#annotations)

# [Saturday 22 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/22/)

All the morning with my painters, who will make an end of all this day I hope. At noon I went to [the Sun tavern](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/500/); on [Fish Street hill](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/175/), to a dinner of [Captn. Teddimans](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/659/), where was my [Lord Inchiquin](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1714/) (who seems to be a very fine person), [Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/), [Captn. Cuttance](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/583/), and one [Mr. Lawrence](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1716/) (a fine gentleman now going to [Algiers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3088/)), and other good company, where we had a very fine dinner, good musique, and a great deal of [wine](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/309/). We staid here very late, at last Sir W. Pen and I home together, he so overcome with wine that he could hardly go; I was forced to lead him through the streets and he was in a very merry and kind mood. I [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) (found my house clear of the workmen and their work ended), my head troubled with wine, and I very merry went to bed, my head akeing all night.

[Read 16 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/22/#annotations)

# [Sunday 23 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/23/)

(Lord’s day). In the morning to [Church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/), where our pew all covered with rosemary and baize. A stranger made a dull sermon.

[Home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and found [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and [maid](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/149/) with much ado had made shift to spit a great [turkey](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/378/) sent me this week from [Charles Carter](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1102/), my old colleague, now minister in Huntingdonshire, but not at all roasted, and so I was fain to stay till two o’clock, and after that to church with my wife, and a good sermon there was, and so home.

All the evening at my [book](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1752/), and so to supper and to bed.

[Read 43 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/23/#annotations)

# [Monday 24 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/24/)

In the morning to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) and [Commissioner Pett](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/708/) (who seldom comes there) told me that he had lately presented a piece of [plate](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7982/) (being a couple of flaggons) to [Mr. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/), but he did not receive them, which also put me upon doing the same too; and so after dinner I went and chose a payre of candlesticks to be made ready for me at [Alderman Backwell’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/967/). To the office again in the afternoon till night, and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and with the painters till 10 at night, making an end of my house and the arch before my door, and so this night I was rid of them and all other work, and my house was made ready against to-morrow being [Christmas day](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/314/). This day [the Princess Royal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/803/) died at Whitehall.

[Read 20 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/24/#annotations)

# [Tuesday 25 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/25/)

([Christmas day](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/314/)). In the morning very much pleased to see my house once more clear of workmen and to be clean, and indeed it is so, far better than it was that I do not repent of my trouble that I have been at.

In the morning to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/), where [Mr. Mills](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1215/) made a very good sermon. After that [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, where [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and I and my brother [Tom](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/236/) (who this morning came to see my wife’s new mantle put on, which do please me very well), to a good shoulder of [mutton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1740/) and a [chicken](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/377/). After dinner to church again, my wife and I, where we had a dull sermon of a stranger, which made me sleep, and so home, and I, before and after supper, to my [lute](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/540/) and [Fuller’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/806/)[History](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1752/), at which I staid all alone in my chamber till 12 at night, and so to bed.

[Read 34 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/25/#annotations)

# [Wednesday 26 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/26/)

In the morning to [Alderman Backwell’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/967/) for the candlesticks for [Mr. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/), but they being not done I went away, and so by coach to [Mr. Crew’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/105/), and there took some money of [Mr. Moore’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/340/) for [my Lord](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), and so to my Lord’s, where I found [Sir Thomas Bond](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1742/) (whom I never saw before) with a message from [the Queen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1399/) about vessells for the carrying over of her goods, and so with him to Mr. Coventry, and thence to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) (being soundly washed going through [the bridge](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/244/)) to [Sir Wm. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) and [Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) (the last of whom took physic to-day), and so I went up to his chamber, and there having made an end of the business I returned to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) by water, and dined with my [Lady Sandwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/), who at table did tell me how much fault was laid upon [Dr. Frazer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1743/) and the rest of the Doctors, for the death of [the Princess](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/803/)!

My Lord did dine this day with [Sir Henry Wright](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/550/), in order to his going to sea with the Queen.

Thence to my father [Bowyer’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/521/) where I met [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), and with her [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) by water.

[Read 18 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/26/#annotations)

# [Thursday 27 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/27/)

In the morning to [Alderman Backwell’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/967/) again, where I found the candlesticks done, and went along with him in his coach to [my Lord’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) and left the candlesticks with [Mr. Shepley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/118/). I staid in the garden talking much with my Lord, who do show me much of his love and do communicate his mind in most things to me, which is my great content.

[Home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) to [Sir W. Batten’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) to dinner, where much and good company. My wife not very well went home, I staid late there seeing them play at [cards](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/797/), and so home to bed.

This afternoon there came in a strange lord to Sir William Batten’s by a mistake and enters discourse with him, so that we could not be rid of him till [Sir Arn. Breames](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1587/) and [Mr. Bens](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1745/) and [Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) fell a-drinking to him till he was drunk, and so sent him away. About the middle of the night I was very ill — I think with eating and drinking too much — and so I was forced to call [the maid](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/149/), who pleased my wife and I in her running up and down so innocently in her smock, and vomited in the bason, and so to sleep, and in the morning was pretty well, only got cold, and so had pain … [in pissing – L&M] as I used to have.

[Read 28 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/27/#annotations)

# [Friday 28 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/28/)

Office day. There all the morning. Dined at [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) alone with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), and so staid within all the afternoon and evening; at my [lute](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/540/), with great pleasure, and so to bed with great content.

[Read 10 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/28/#annotations)

# [Saturday 29 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/29/)

Within all the morning. Several people to speak with me; [Mr. Shepley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/118/) for 100 _l._; [Mr. Kennard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1677/) and [Warren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1748/), the merchant, about [deals](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4992/) for [my Lord](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/). [Captain Robert Blake](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/663/) lately come from [the Straights](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3260/) about some Florence [Wine](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/309/) for my Lord, and with him I went to [Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/), who offering me a barrel of [oysters](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/373/) I took them both [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to my house (having by chance a good piece of roast [beef](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/381/) at the fire for dinner), and there they dined with me, and sat talking all the afternoon-good company. Thence to [Alderman Backwell’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/967/) and took a brave state-plate and cupp in lieu of the candlesticks that I had the other day and carried them by coach to my Lord’s and left them there. And so back to [my father’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/154/) and saw [my mother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/282/), and so to my [uncle Fenner’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/749/), whither my father came to me, and there we talked and drank, and so away; I home with my father, he telling me what bad wives both my [cozen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1105/)[Joyces](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1749/) make to [their](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1107/)[husbands](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1090/), which I much wondered at. After talking of [my sister’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1568/) coming to me next week, I went home and to bed.

[Read 23 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/29/#annotations)

# [Sunday 30 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/30/)

(Lord’s day). Lay long in bed, and being up, I went with [Will](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1082/) to [my Lord’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), calling in at many churches in my way. There I found [Mr. Shepley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/118/), in his Venetian cap, taking physique in his chamber, and with him I sat till dinner.

My Lord dined abroad and [my Lady](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/) in her chamber, so [Mr. Hetly](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/858/), [Child](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1253/) and I dined together, and after dinner Mr. Child and I spent some time at the [lute](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/540/), and so promising to prick me some lessons to my [theorbo](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/457/) he went away to see [Henry Laws](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/866/), who lies very sick.

I to [the Abby](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1012/) and walked there, seeing the great confusion of people that come there to hear the [organs](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1586/). So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), calling in at [my father’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/154/), but staid not, my father and [mother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/282/) being both forth.

At home I fell a-reading of [Fuller’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/806/)[Church History](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1752/) till it was late, and so to bed.

[Read 27 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/30/#annotations)

# [Monday 31 December 1660](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/31/)

At [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) all the morning and after that [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and not staying to dine I went out, and in [Paul’s Church-yard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/182/) I bought the play of [“Henry the Fourth,”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5442/) and so went to [the new Theatre](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1611/) (only calling at [Mr. Crew’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/105/) and eat a bit with the people there at dinner) and saw it acted; but my expectation being too great, it did not please me, as otherwise I believe it would; and my having a book, I believe did spoil it a little.

That being done I went to [my Lord’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), where I found him private at [cards](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/797/) with my [Lord Lauderdale](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/767/) and some persons of honour. So [Mr. Shepley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/118/) and I over to [Harper’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/241/), and there drank a pot or two, and so parted. [My boy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1248/) taking a cat home with him from my Lord’s, which [Sarah](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5611/) had given him for [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), we being much troubled with mice.

At [Whitehall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) inquiring for a coach, there was a Frenchman with one eye that was going my way, so he and I hired the coach between us and he set me down in [Fenchurch Street](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1075/). Strange how the fellow, without asking, did tell me all what he was, and how he had ran away from his father and come into England to serve [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/), and now going back again.

Home and to bed.

# Diary entries from December 1668

# [Tuesday 1 December 1668](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/01/)

Up, and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where sat all the morning, and at noon with my people to dinner, and so to the office, very busy till night, and then [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and made [my boy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7767/) read to me [Wilkins’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1626/)[Reall Character](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10020/), which do please me mightily, and so after supper to bed with great pleasure and content with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/). This day I hear of poor [Mr. Clerke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5255/), the solicitor, being dead, of a cold, after being not above two days ill, which troubles me mightily, poor man!

[Read 4 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/01/#annotations)

# [Wednesday 2 December 1668](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/02/)

Up, and at [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) all the morning upon some accounts of [Sir D. Gawden](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/994/), and at noon abroad with [W. Hewer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1082/), thinking to have found [Mr. Wren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8019/) at [Captain Cox’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3376/), to have spoke something to him about doing a favour for Will’s uncle [Steventon](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6292/), but missed him. And so back [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and abroad with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), the first time that ever I rode in my own coach, which do make my heart rejoice, and praise God, and pray him to bless it to me and continue it. So she and I to the [King’s playhouse](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/475/), and there sat to avoid seeing [Knepp](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9483/) in a box above where [Mrs. Williams](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8925/) happened to be, and there saw [“The Usurper;”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7124/) a pretty good play, in all but what is designed to resemble [Cromwell](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/796/) and [Hugh Peters](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1273/), which is mighty silly. The play done, we to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/); where my wife staid while I up to the [Duchesse’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1402/) and [Queen’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2381/) side, to speak with the [Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/): and here saw all the ladies, and heard the silly discourse of [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/), with his people about him, telling a story of my [Lord Rochester’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5344/) having of his clothes stole, while he was with a wench; and his gold all gone, but his clothes found afterwards stuffed into a feather bed by the wench that stole them. I spoke with the Duke of York, just as he was set down to supper with the King, about our sending of victuals to [Sir Thomas Allen’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1204/) fleet hence to [Cales](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3766/) [Cadiz] to meet him. And so back to my wife in my coach, and so with great content and joy home, where I made [my boy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7767/) to make an end of the [Reall Character](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10020/), which I begun a great while ago, and do please me infinitely, and indeed is a most worthy labour, and I think mighty easy, though my eyes make me unable to attempt any thing in it.

To-day I hear that [Mr. Ackworth’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/814/) cause went for him at [Guildhall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/129/), against his accusers, which I am well enough pleased with.

[Read 11 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/02/#annotations)

# [Thursday 3 December 1668](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/03/)

Up betimes, and by water with [W. Hewer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1082/) to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), and there to [Mr. Wren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8019/), who gives me but small hopes of the favour I hoped for [Mr. Steventon](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6292/), Will’s uncle, of having leave, being upon the point of death, to surrender his place, which do trouble me, but I will do what I can. So back again to [the Office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), [Sir Jer. Smith](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6415/) with me; who is a silly, prating, talking man; but he tells me what he hears, that [Holmes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/930/) and [Spragg](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5954/) now rule all with the [Duke of Buckingham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2558/), as to seabusiness, and will be great men: but he do prophesy what will be the fruit of it; so I do. So to the Office, where we sat all the morning; and at noon [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, and then abroad again, with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), to the [Duke of York’s playhouse](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2935/), and saw [“The Unfortunate Lovers;”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7344/) a mean play, I think, but some parts very good, and excellently acted. We sat under the boxes, and saw the fine ladies; among others, my [Lady Kerneguy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8364/), who is most devilishly painted. And so home, it being mighty pleasure to go alone with my poor wife, in a coach of our own, to a play, and makes us appear mighty great, I think, in the world; at least, greater than ever I could, or my friends for me, have once expected; or, I think, than ever any of my family ever yet lived, in my memory, but my cozen [Pepys](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2807/) in [Salisbury Court](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/161/). So to the office, and thence home to supper and to bed.

[Read 11 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/03/#annotations)

# [Friday 4 December 1668](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/04/)

Up, and with [W. Hewer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1082/) by water to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), and there did wait as usual upon the [Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/), where, upon discoursing something touching the [Ticket](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4086/)-Office, which by letter the [Board](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/482/) did give the Duke of York their advice, to be put upon [Lord Brouncker](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4135/), [Sir J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/) did foolishly rise up and complain of [the Office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and his being made nothing of; and this before [Sir Thomas Littleton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10174/), who would be glad of this difference among us, which did trouble me mightily; and therefore I did forbear to say what I otherwise would have thought fit for me to say on this occasion, upon so impertinent a speech as this doting fool made — but, I say, I let it alone, and contented myself that it went as I advised, as to the Duke of York’s judgment, in the thing disputed. And so thence away, my coach meeting me there and carrying me to several places to do little jobs, which is a mighty convenience, and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), where by invitation I find my [aunt Wight](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/995/), who looked over all our house, and is mighty pleased with it, and indeed it is now mighty handsome, and rich in furniture. By and by comes [my uncle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/911/), and then to dinner, where a [venison pasty](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/384/) and very merry, and after dinner I carried [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and her to [Smithfield](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2595/), where they sit in the coach, while [Mr. Pickering](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/612/), who meets me there, and I, and W. Hewer, and a friend of his, a jockey, did go about to see several pairs of horses, for my coach; but it was late, and we agreed on none, but left it to another time: but here I do see instances of a piece of craft and cunning that I never dreamed of, concerning the buying and choosing of horses. So Mr. Pickering, to whom I am much beholden for his kindness herein, and I parted; and I with my people home, where I left them, and I to the office, to meet about some business of [Sir W. Warren’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1748/) accounts, where I vexed to see how ill all the [Comptroller’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/485/) business is likely to go on, so long as ever [Sir J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/) lives; and so troubled I was, that I thought it a good occasion for me to give my thoughts of it in writing, and therefore wrote a letter at the Board, by the help of [a tube](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13543/), to Lord Brouncker, and did give it him, which I kept a copy of, and it may be of use to me hereafter to shew, in this matter. This being done, I home to my aunt, who supped with us, and my uncle also: and a good-humoured woman she is, so that I think we shall keep her acquaintance; but mighty proud she is of her wedding-ring, being lately set with [diamonds](https://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/14124/); cost her about 12 _l._: and I did commend it mightily to her, but do not think it very suitable for one of our quality. After supper they home, and we to bed.

[Read 17 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/04/#annotations)

# [Saturday 5 December 1668](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/05/)

Up, after a little talk with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), which troubled me, she being ever since our late difference mighty watchful of sleep and dreams, and will not be persuaded but I do dream of [Deb.](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/), and do tell me that I speak in my dreams and that this night I did cry, Huzzy, and it must be she, and now and then I start otherwise than I used to do, she says, which I know not, for I do not know that I dream of her more than usual, though I cannot deny that my thoughts waking do run now and then against my will and judgment upon her, for that only is wanting to undo me, being now in every other thing as to my mind most happy, and may still be so but for my own fault, if I be catched loving any body but my wife again. So up and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and at noon to dinner, and thence to office, where late, mighty busy, and despatching much business, settling papers in my own office, and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to supper, and to bed. No news stirring, but that my [Lord of Ormond](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1221/) is likely to go to Ireland again, which do shew that the [Duke of Buckingham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2558/) do not rule all so absolutely; and that, however, we shall speedily have more changes in the Navy: and it is certain that the [Nonconformists](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/666/) do now preach openly in houses, in many places, and among others the house that was heretofore [Sir G. Carteret’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1018/), in [Leadenhall Streete](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3369/), and have ready access to [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/). And now the great dispute is, whether this [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/) or another; and my great design, if I continue in the Navy, is to get myself to be a Parliament-man.

[Read 12 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/05/#annotations)

# [Sunday 6 December 1668](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/06/)

(Lord’s day). Up, and with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/); which pleases me mightily, I being full of fear that she would never go to church again, after she had declared to me that she was a [Roman Catholique](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/306/). But though I do verily think she fears God, and is truly and sincerely righteous, yet I do see she is not so strictly so a Catholique as not to go to church with me, which pleases me mightily. Here [Mills](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1215/) made a lazy sermon, upon Moses’s meeknesse, and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and my wife and I alone to dinner, and then she to read [a little book](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13093/) concerning speech in general, a translation late out of French; a most excellent piece as ever I read, proving a soul in man, and all the ways and secrets by which nature teaches speech in man, which do please me most infinitely to read. By and by my wife to church, and I to [my Office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) to complete my Journall for the last three days, and so home to my chamber to settle some papers, and so to spend the evening with my wife and [W. Hewer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1082/) talking over the business of the Office, and particularly my own Office, how I will make it, and it will become, in a little time, an Office of ease, and not slavery, as it hath for so many years been. So to supper, and to bed.

# [Monday 7 December 1668](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/07/)

Up by candlelight, the first time I have done so this winter, but I had lost my labour so often to visit [Sir W. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/), and not visited him so long, that I was resolved to get time enough, and so up, and with [W. Hewer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1082/), it being the first frosty day we have had this winter, did walk it very well to W. Coventry’s, and there alone with him an hour talking of the Navy, which he pities, but says he hath no more mind to be found meddling with the Navy, lest it should do it hurt, as well as him, to be found to meddle with it. So to talk of general things: and telling him that, with all these doings, he, I thanked God, stood yet; he told me, Yes, but that he thought his continuing in, did arise from his enemies my [Lord of Buckingham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2558/) and [Arlington’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5520/) seeing that he cared so little if he was out; and he do protest to me that he is as weary of the Treasury, as ever he was of the Navy. He tells me that he do believe that their heat is over almost, as to the Navy, there being now none left of the old stock but my [Lord Brouncker](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4135/), [J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/), who is ready to leave the world, and myself. But he tells me that he do foresee very great wants and great disorders by reason thereof; insomuch, as he is represented to [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) by his enemies as a melancholy man, and one that is still prophesying ill events, so as the King called him Visionaire, which being told him, he said he answered the party, that, whatever he foresaw, he was not afeard as to himself of any thing, nor particularly of my Lord Arlington, so much as the Duke of Buckingham hath been, nor of the Duke of Buckingham, so much as my Lord Arlington at this time is. But he tells me that he hath been always looked upon as a melancholy man; whereas, others that would please the King do make him believe that all is safe: and so he hath heard my [Lord Chancellor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/) openly say to the King, that he was now a glorious prince, and in a glorious condition, because of some one accident that hath happened, or some one rub that hath been removed; “when,” says W. Coventry, “they reckoned their one good meal, without considering that there was nothing left in the cup board for to-morrow.” After this and other discourse of this kind, I away, and walked to my [Lord Sandwich’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), and walked with him to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), and took a quarter of an hour’s walk in the garden with him, which I had not done for so much time with him since his coming into England; and talking of his own condition, and particularly of the world’s talk of his going to [Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2783/). I find, if his conditions can be made profitable and safe as to money, he would go, but not else; but, however, will seem not averse to it, because of facilitating his other accounts now depending, which he finds hard to get through, but yet hath some hopes, the King, he says, speaking very kindly to him. Thence to a [Committee of Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5243/), and so with W. Hewer to Westminster to [Sir R. Longs](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6083/) office, and so to the [Temple](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/131/), but did nothing, [the Auditor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5698/) not being within, and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, and after dinner out again with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) to the Temple, and up and down to do a little business, and back again, and so to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and did a little business, and so home, and W. Hewer with me, to read and talk, and so to supper, and then to bed in mighty good humour. This afternoon, passing through [Queen’s Street](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/12247/), I saw pass by our coach on foot [Deb.](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/), which, God forgive me, did put me into some new thoughts of her, and for her, but durst not shew them, and I think my wife did not see her, but I did get my thoughts free of her soon as I could.

# [Tuesday 8 December 1668](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/08/)

Up, and [Sir H. Cholmly](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5179/) betimes with me, about some accounts and moneys due to him: and he gone, I to [the Office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where sat all the morning; and here, among other things, breaks out the storm [W. Hewer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1082/) and I have long expected from [the Surveyor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7120/),—[Colonel Middleton.]— about W. Hewer’s conspiring to get a contract, to the burdening of the stores with [kerseys](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13109/) and cottons, of which he hath often complained, and lately more than ever; and now he did it by a most scandalous letter to [the Board](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/482/), reflecting on my Office: and, by discourse, it fell to such high words between him and me, as can hardly ever be forgot; I declaring I would believe W. Hewer as soon as him, and laying the fault, if there be any, upon himself; he, on the other hand, vilifying of my word and W. Hewer’s, calling him knave, and that if he were his clerk, he should lose his ears. At last, I closed the business for this morning with making the thing ridiculous, as it is, and he swearing that [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) should have right in it, or he would lose his place. The Office was cleared of all but ourselves and W. Hewer; but, however, the world did by the beginning see what it meant, and it will, I believe, come to high terms between us, which I am sorry for, to have any blemish laid upon me or mine, at this time, though never so unduly, for fear of giving occasion to my real discredit: and therefore I was not only all the rest of the morning vexed, but so went [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, where my [wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) tells me of my [Lord Orrery’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/954/) new play [“Tryphon,”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13110/) at the [Duke of York’s house](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2935/), which, however, I would see, and therefore put a bit of meat in our mouths, and went thither; where, with much ado, at half-past one, we got into a blind hole in the 18 _d._ place, above stairs, where we could not hear well, but the house infinite full, but the prologue most silly, and the play, though admirable, yet no pleasure almost in it, because just the very same design, and words, and sense, and plot, as every one of his plays have, any one of which alone would be held admirable, whereas so many of the same design and fancy do but dull one another; and this, I perceive, is the sense of every body else, as well as myself, who therefore showed but little pleasure in it. So home, mighty hot, and my mind mightily out of order, so as I could not eat any supper, or sleep almost all night, though I spent till twelve at night with W. Hewer to consider of our business: and we find it not only most free from any blame of our side, but so horrid scandalous on the other, to make so groundless a complaint, and one so shameful to him, that it could not but let me see that there is no need of my being troubled; but such is the weakness of my nature, that I could not help it, which vexes me, showing me how unable I am to live with difficulties.

# [Wednesday 9 December 1668](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/09/)

Up, and to [the Office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), but did little there, my mind being still uneasy, though more and more satisfied that there is no occasion for it; but abroad with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) to [the Temple](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/131/), where I met with [Auditor Wood’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5698/) clerk, and did some business with him, and so to see [Mr. Spong](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1060/), and found him out by [Southampton Market](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10216/), and there carried my wife, and up to his chamber, a bye place, but with a good prospect of the fields; and there I had most infinite pleasure, not only with his ingenuity in general, but in particular with his shewing me the use of the [Parallelogram](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/12993/), by which he drew in a quarter of an hour before me, in little, from a great, a most neat map of England — that is, all the outlines, which gives me infinite pleasure, and foresight of pleasure, I shall have with it; and therefore desire to have that which I have bespoke, made. Many other pretty things he showed us, and did give me [a glass bubble](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13111/), to try the strength of liquors with. This done, and having spent 6 _d._ in [ale](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/450/) in the coach, at the door of the [Bull Inn](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/12498/), with the innocent master of the house, a Yorkshireman, for his letting us go through his house, we away to [Hercules Pillars](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1432/), and there eat a bit of meat: and so, with all speed, back to the [Duke of York’s house](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2935/), where mighty full again; but we come time enough to have a good place in the pit, and did hear [this new play](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13110/) again, where, though I better understood it than before, yet my sense of it and pleasure was just the same as yesterday, and no more, nor any body else’s about us. So took our coach and [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), having now little pleasure to look about me to see the fine faces, for fear of displeasing my wife, whom I take great comfort now, more than ever, in pleasing; and it is a real joy to me. So home, and to my Office, where spent an hour or two; and so home to my wife, to supper and talk, and so to bed.

# [Thursday 10 December 1668](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/10/)

Up, and to [the Office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where busy all the morning: [Middleton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7120/) not there, so no words or looks of him. At noon, [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner; and so to the Office, and there all the afternoon busy; and at night [W. Hewer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1082/) home with me; and we think we have got matter enough to make Middleton appear a coxcomb. But it troubled me to have [Sir W. Warren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1748/) meet me at night, going out of the Office home, and tell me that Middleton do intend to complain to the [Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/): but, upon consideration of the business, I did go to bed, satisfied that it was best for me that he should; and so my trouble was over, and to bed, and slept well.
